summary: Full regression on Brasil Minis PostgreSQL rewrite. Wrote pytest suite (41 tests) covering health, catalog+filters+sort+related, auth (cookies, /me, refresh, logout, forgot/reset, Bearer, brute force), RBAC (admin stats 401/403/200), coupons (BRASIL10/MINIS20/FRETEGRATIS + invalid), orders w/ atomic stock decrement + oversell rejection + concurrent no-negative-stock + coupon+shipping, account (profile, password, addresses), favorites idempotent, reviews (recompute rating, auth-required), admin CRUD (products, orders, customers, banners). 40/41 backend tests PASS. Frontend smoke: home banner+products load, /produtos lists 28 items with filters, admin login→ /conta then /admin dashboard renders stats (R$4.059,13, 14 pedidos, 28 produtos, 2 clientes). Only failure: brute force lockout not enforced end-to-end because request.client.host is the ingress pod IP which rotates across ~2 pods, splitting login attempts across identifiers.

critical.issue: Brute force protection bypassable: identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}" uses the ingress pod IP (verified 10.79.139.10 / 10.79.139.11 alternating), so attempts split across pods and MAX_ATTEMPTS is never reached per identifier. Manually observed: 8 consecutive wrong logins all return 401 (never 429). Fix: extract real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first hop) or key only by lowercased email.

issues: /api/auth/me on public pages returns 401 for anonymous visitors — expected behavior but produces two console errors on every page load; consider guarding the call or suppressing 401 log noise.

action_items: Fix brute-force identifier: use X-Forwarded-For (real client IP) or drop IP from key so lockout works across ingress pods. Currently 6+ wrong logins for the same email still return 401 instead of 429.
Optional: skip /api/auth/me on public routes when no cookie is present to reduce 401 console noise.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py: rate-limit identifier uses raw request.client.host — behind K8s ingress this is the proxy IP; use request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', request.client.host).split(',')[0].strip().

auth.py: on wrong password the code sets locked_until on EVERY failed attempt (even the first), which sort of works but means the lockout timer keeps refreshing. Consider only setting locked_until when count reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS.
admin.py stats: revenue is computed by loading all orders into memory (db.query(Order).all() twice); replace with SQL func.sum(Order.total) and date_trunc for revenue_series to scale.
orders.py / order_service.py: build_mock_payment attached only on create; GET /api/orders/{id} does not surface payment info — acceptable for MVP but document.
catalog.py: Product.badges.contains([badge]) requires JSONB column with GIN or full scan; ensure index on JSONB or precomputed columns for scale.
seed.py runs on every startup; make sure it is idempotent for products (looks OK) but be aware AUTO_CREATE_TABLES=true in preview will hide missing Alembic migrations.

context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py is authoritative regression. To re-run: cd /app/backend && pytest tests/backend_test.py -v. Brute force test will keep failing until identifier is fixed. If auth logic is changed, verify /api/auth/me still works with both httpOnly cookie AND Authorization: Bearer header. Concurrent stock test spawns 10 admin-login sessions in parallel — this counts as brute-force-safe login (correct password) so unrelated to lockout.
rca of the issue: Brute force lockout FAIL RCA: Selected sample from login_attempts table showed two rows for the same email — one per ingress pod IP (10.79.139.10 with count=5, 10.79.139.11 with count=3). Identifier `{ip}:{email}` therefore never reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS in a single row when ingress round-robins across pods. Reproduction: `for i in {1..8}; do curl -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -d '{"email":"any@x.com","password":"wrong"}'; done` — all return 401. Mitigation: read X-Forwarded-For (Kubernetes ingress sets it) or key identifier only on email (with per-IP as secondary layer).
